name: Mattathias
overview: Mattathias is a male figure noted in Scripture as being in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Luke 3:25. There is no additional tribal or personal background information provided. His significance is primarily tied to his genealogical position within the Messianic line.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattathias means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's providence. This proper name highlights the divine blessing implied in his identity, as noted in Luke 3:25.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mattathias as the father of Joseph and the grandfather of Amos, establishing a direct paternal lineage. These relationships are explicitly and implicitly referenced in Luke 3:25, underscoring his role within a family line significant to the Messianic genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Mattathias holds importance as an ancestor in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, emphasizing God's sovereign plan in preserving the Messianic line through successive generations. His mention in Luke 3:25 connects him to the fulfillment of biblical prophecy concerning the Messiah's descent, affirming the continuity of God's redemptive work through history.
